title: LEARNING HOW TO DANCE BWOLA (Acoli royal dance)

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor leads community members in traditional Bwola dance practice outdoors. The teaching style is participatory and communal, with group singing and drumming accompanying the steps.

lesson_structure.note: Group forms line and begins singing and dancing outdoors
Group bends down and steps in unison with drums
Larger group forms circle around drummers
Young drummers and dancers practice together

steps_taught.name: Bwola basic step
steps_taught.description: Rhythmic stepping and body lowering to drum beat

what_works: Call and response singing helps maintain rhythm
Large group setting allows learners to follow peers
what_hinders: No verbal breakdown or counting provided

evidence_segments.observation: Dancers moving in a line with rattles and small drums
Dancers lowering upper bodies while keeping rhythm with feet

extraction.distinctive_method: Traditional community-based learning through collective dancing and singing rather than verbal instruction.
